key_insight: General-purpose LLMs outperform domain-specific pretrained models in the reported alloy-property benchmarks, with further gains from prior-model numerical estimates.
engineering_relevance: Combining general-purpose LLMs with existing predictors and carefully selected reference data could reduce the cost of alloy-property screening.
method: Benchmark general-purpose LLMs against SteelBERT, MatSciBERT, and SciBERT across Ti, steel, HEA, and Al datasets.
Prompt DeepSeek V3.1 and Gemini-2.5-Flash with CatBoost or SteelBERT estimates to guide prediction corrections.
Assess similarity-based reference selection and compare self-reported confidence with prediction error.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that using only 5% of high-similarity training references achieves performance comparable to using the full training set.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify errors or out-of-distribution severity, so robustness to substantially different alloy compositions remains unclear.
paper_title: Quantifying out-of-distribution data severity with Wasserstein distances: benchmarking large language models for alloy property prediction
